questions.question: When loading liquid cargo, you should consider the ____.
questions.explanation: When loading liquid, consider how much it will expand during transport, its weight, and legal weight limits for your vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Ignore the report and find any issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and rely only on the report.

questions.explanation: Review any previous inspection reports on your vehicle. The carrier should have fixed any problems noted in the report.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a cab from:
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can:

options.text: Allow poisonous fumes into the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow poisonous fumes into the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: On a slippery road, a driver should:
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Turn gently and do not pass other vehicles unless necessary.

questions.question: When loading a tank divided by bulkheads with liquid cargo, most weight should go:

options.text: In the top of the tank.
In the middle of the tank.
In the rear of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle of the tank.
questions.explanation: When filling a tank with bulkheads, do not put too much weight on the front or rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: Regrooved tires are:

options.text: Allowed only on the front of a bus.
Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
Not allowed anywhere on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed only on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not allowed on the front of a bus.

questions.question: Which is NOT an example of a distracted person motorists should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to someone in the vehicle
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Drivers in conversations may not pay full attention to the road. Children may dart into the road without looking. Be careful near road workers to keep them and distracted drivers safe. A person sitting on a bench is not a traffic concern.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Someone must always be at the nozzle controlling fuel flow.

questions.question: Mismatched tire sizes:

options.text: Can be used only on a front axle.
Can be used only on a trailer's axles.

questions.explanation: All tires on a vehicle should be the same size. Check that your tires match when inspecting your vehicle.

questions.question: When you check a power steering system, you should make sure that:

options.text: The hoses are connected to the battery.
The hoses have no fluid in them.

questions.explanation: Check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level in a power steering system. Look for leaks and fix them before you drive.

questions.question: Before driving a tank truck, you should NOT:

options.text: Assume that pipes, connections, and hoses have no leaks.
Check the tank for dents or leaks.
Make sure the valves are in the right positions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume that pipes, connections, and hoses have no leaks.
questions.explanation: Before driving a tank truck, check for dangerous leaks. Inspect the tank, pipes, connections, and hoses. Check that all valves are in the correct positions before loading, unloading, or moving the vehicle.

questions.question: What can the "crack-the-whip" effect cause?
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can cause a trailer to tip over during a lane change. To prevent this, make lane changes slowly and safely.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and get rest. Driving tired is dangerous. Do not rely on caffeine to stay awake.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. To avoid rolling over, drive slowly on entrance ramps, exit ramps, and corners. Avoid quick lane changes when towing a trailer.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous if your truck rolls backward when you start to accelerate?

options.text: The truck is not built to go backward.
You could hit a vehicle behind you.
You could lose your place in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: To avoid hitting something behind you, make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when you start from a stop. With a manual transmission, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake.

questions.question: When driving at highway speeds, look ahead about ____ from your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Watch the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead to see hazards early. At highway speeds, this equals about a quarter mile.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat and makes a loud noise, the truck will be affected:

options.text: Only if the flat tire is in the front.
Only if the truck is carrying cargo.

questions.explanation: There is a short delay between when a tire fails and when you feel it affect the truck. Because of this delay, you might think the noise came from another vehicle.

questions.question: The faster you drive:

options.text: The shorter it takes to stop.
The longer it takes to stop.
The easier it is to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer it takes to stop.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. Brake based on your speed.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Usually happens when driving faster than 65 mph.
Can happen with just a little water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen with just a little water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip and slide on a layer of water. You do not need a lot of water on the road for this to happen.
